Mars Reel is a 500 Global portfolio company operating consumer web and streaming products. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or technical documentation; this profile captures its public identity and consumer link surface only.

providers.name: Onefootball
providers.description: Onefootball is a Berlin-based digital football (soccer) media platform that aggregates news, live scores, match coverage, video highlights, and streaming (OneFootball TV) for a global audience across iOS, Android, and the web. Backed by Earlybird and Union Square Ventures, the company partners with clubs, leagues, and publishers to distribute content and operates an official merchandise store and a Web3/club ecosystem. Onefootball does not publish a public developer API or partner developer portal; content ingestion for partners is handled via WordPress REST and private editorial integrations rather than an open, documented API surface.

providers.name: Religion of Sports
providers.description: Religion of Sports is an Emmy Award-winning sports media and entertainment production studio founded in 2017 by Tom Brady, Michael Strahan and Gotham Chopra, headquartered in Santa Monica, California and operating as The Religion of Sports Media, Inc. The company produces premium non-fiction film, documentary series and branded content that examine why sports matter, distributed through Netflix, HBO, Paramount+, ESPN, Apple TV+, Showtime, Fox Sports and NBC Sports, with titles including Simone Biles Rising, In the Arena: Serena Williams, Made for March, 5-Star and Alex vs. ARod. It raised a $50M Series B led by Shamrock Capital in June 2022 to build a non-fiction studio arm and expand into new formats and non-sports categories. Its public surface is a marketing and press site; the company operates no developer program, publishes no API documentation, and exposes no machine-readable contract.

providers.name: i-Brain Tech
providers.description: i-Brain Tech is a neuroscience company building a brain-controlled training platform for sports performance. Its core product is a video game driven exclusively by an athlete's brain impulses through motor-imagery and neurofeedback, requiring no physical movement. The platform is applied to three areas: post-injury neuromuscular recovery and return-to-play readiness, player development through cognitive and tactical training without physical strain, and cognitive assessment that surfaces mental resilience, attention, and endurance from real brain data. Elite football clubs including Real Sociedad, Juventus FC, CD Leganes, Olympique Lyonnais, S.L. Benfica, and Seattle Reign FC use the platform. i-Brain Tech is a Techstars portfolio company. It currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Gym Class VR
providers.description: Gym Class VR (operating as "Gym Class" by IRL Studios) is a social virtual reality sports gaming platform for Meta Quest headsets and mobile devices, offering multiplayer basketball, baseball, football, boxing, paintball, and soccer experiences where players compete, socialize, and create and share their own games. The top-rated sports title on the Meta Quest Store with a 4.8-star average across 53,000+ ratings, the company holds licensing agreements with the NBA and Major League Baseball, expanded to mobile in 2026, and has raised over $8M from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Y Combinator, and NBA players. It is a consumer VR entertainment product with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Overtime
providers.description: Overtime is a sports media and entertainment company building disruptive, digital-first sports leagues and intellectual property aimed at the next generation of fans and athletes. It operates branded leagues including Overtime Elite (OTE) basketball, OT7 seven-on-seven football, and OT Select women's basketball, and reaches nearly 100 million followers across social platforms. Backed by a16z, Overtime generates revenue through sponsorships, merchandise, media rights, and brand partnerships, reimagining how Gen Z engages with sports through content-first entertainment.

providers.name: Player's Health
providers.description: Player's Health is an insurance and athlete-safety technology company founded in 2016 and based in Minneapolis, Minnesota, serving youth sports organizations, fitness facilities, schools, and collegiate athletic programs. The platform combines specialty insurance products (general liability, sexual abuse and molestation liability, accident medical, directors and officers, equipment and property, cyber, and employee benefits) with athlete-safety and risk-management tooling including coach credentialing and background checks, injury and incident reporting, investigations, mental-health support, and training. Player's Health operates login-gated web portals for claims, certificates of insurance, and safety/compliance (SafetyHub) rather than a public developer API. It is a Techstars-backed company surfaced through the API Evangelist network and profiled here for discovery.

providers.name: Bleacher Report
providers.description: Bleacher Report is a digital sports media company headquartered in San Francisco and owned by Warner Bros. Discovery (Turner Sports). Founded in 2007, it delivers sports news, live scores, highlights, video, and community-driven commentary across the web and its iOS and Android applications, spanning the NFL, NBA, MLB, soccer, and other leagues. Bleacher Report maintains a public GitHub organization with open source engineering projects but does not publish a public developer API program; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Fox Corporation
providers.description: Fox Corporation (NASDAQ: FOXA, FOX) is a US media company spun out of 21st Century Fox in 2019 when the rest of the business was sold to Disney. Per the company website, "Fox Corporation produces and distributes compelling news, sports, and entertainment content through its primary iconic domestic brands" — Fox News Media (Fox News Channel, Fox Business Network, Fox News Digital, Fox News Audio, Fox Weather), Fox Sports (FS1, FS2, Big Ten Network, Fox Deportes, Fox Bet partnerships), Fox Entertainment, Fox Television Stations, and the Tubi Media Group (Tubi free ad-supported streaming, Credible). In May 2024 Fox acquired Mexican sports-betting and casino operator Caliente.mx, expanding its sports-and-wagering footprint into Latin America. Fox does not publish a public developer portal or REST API surface for the parent corporation — programmatic distribution is delivered via per-brand RSS / Atom feeds (Fox News, Fox Business, Fox Sports, Fox Weather), the Tubi Media Group open source projects on GitHub (github.com/Tubitv, 53 public repositories), and direct B2B advertising and content-syndication relationships rather than self-serve API signup. This apis.yml therefore catalogs the public RSS surface, Tubi engineering OSS, and the corporate/brand web properties.

providers.name: SwingVision
providers.description: SwingVision is an AI-powered tennis and pickleball platform built by a team of A.I. experts from Tesla and Apple, venture-backed by Tennis Australia, Sony, and Techstars. Its mobile app processes video on-device with computer vision to deliver automated line calling, scoring, match stats, and highlight reels from a single phone or tablet camera. SwingVision is a consumer application and does not publish a public developer API; its api.swing.vision backend is private and undocumented, with data export offered through the app as video and spreadsheet files.

providers.name: Audacy
providers.description: Audacy, Inc. is a U.S. multi-platform audio and entertainment company that operates the country's second-largest radio group alongside the Audacy streaming app, a major podcast network, and the Amperwave audio ad-tech and distribution platform. Formerly known as Entercom (rebranded to Audacy on March 30, 2021), the company filed prepackaged Chapter 11 bankruptcy on January 7, 2024 and emerged on September 30, 2024 as a privately held company after equitizing approximately $1.6 billion of funded debt and reducing total debt from roughly $1.9 billion to $350 million. The current portfolio spans ~230 radio brands across 47 markets, 200+ million monthly listeners, ~2 billion annual podcast downloads, and the Cadence13, Pineapple Street Studios, Podcorn, and BetMGM Network (formerly BetQL) audio brands. There is no public developer API, no published OpenAPI, and no GitHub organization with public repositories; integration is brokered through ad sales, programmatic marketplaces, and the Amperwave platform.

providers.name: AlmostApps
providers.description: AlmostApps is a Sacramento, California sports-gaming studio founded in 2022 that builds free-to-play mobile entertainment experiences for sports fans, blending casual gameplay with real-life sports scores and stats. Its flagship product, Tailgate, is a free-to-play mobile sports entertainment app designed to enhance the game-day experience for casual sports enthusiasts. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Parade Ventures. AlmostApps is a consumer application company and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDK, or API documentation; only a marketing site with Terms of Service and Privacy Policy is publicly available. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a company lead.

providers.name: Instacoach
providers.description: Instacoach is an AI-powered baseball training app that generates personalized, on-demand workout programs for athletes across hitting, pitching, arm care, fielding, catching, lifting, and mental performance. Programs are built by college and pro athletes and adapt to the user's equipment and goals, with short guided drills, progress tracking, and stat logging. It is delivered as consumer iOS and Android apps plus a web experience, and also offers team training programs for coaches. Sector: consumer sports/fitness technology. Backed by GGV Capital. No public developer API surface was found during enrichment (no api./developer./docs. host, no /.well-known, llms.txt, or OpenAPI).

providers.name: Jump
providers.description: Jump is a unified fan experience and ticketing platform built exclusively for professional sports teams. It combines primary and resale ticketing, team-branded mobile apps and websites, marketing and messaging, loyalty, fan identity and wallet, point-of-sale and scanning, dynamic pricing, and a unified fan-data foundation into a single system that teams own and control. Jump also embeds agentic AI agents to automate pricing, inventory, and revenue operations. It serves teams across the NBA, MLB, WNBA, NWSL, USL, and NCAA and is backed by Battery Ventures, Forerunner Ventures, Index Ventures, and Menlo Ventures. Jump connects to the tools teams already use through integration APIs, but publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI, or self-serve API documentation.

providers.name: Season Share
providers.description: Season Share (SeasonShare) is a ticketing technology platform for sports and entertainment venues. Its subscription-pass, last-minute, student, and credit-based products — Pass, Flow, Flex, and LivePass — help teams and venues reach younger fans, capture first-party data, and build recurring ticket revenue. It reports $100M+ in ticket inventory delivered and 1.5M tickets purchased, and is used by 30+ franchises including the Sacramento Kings, New Jersey Devils, Arizona Diamondbacks, and Nashville Predators. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company; no public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: SuperQuickQuestion
providers.description: SuperQuickQuestion (SQQ) is a fan-engagement platform that hosts brief, 60-second one-on-one live video interactions between fans and celebrities, athletes, and musicians. It is web-based with no app download required, uses industry-standard encryption, and removes traditional event logistics (travel, hotels, agent back-and-forth) so talent only needs WiFi and a camera device while fans receive brand- or team-sponsored free access. Early clients include professional sports organizations such as the Washington Wizards, Cleveland Browns, Washington Mystics, Wrexham AFC, and talent like Ric Flair. No public API, developer portal, or SDK surface is currently published; this remains a consumer product profile.

providers.name: ATC (Alquila tu cancha)
providers.description: ATC (Alquila Tu Cancha) is an Argentine sports-technology company, founded in 2020, that operates LATAM's leading platform for booking amateur sports venues — courts for football, padel, tennis and more — alongside cloud management software for the clubs and complexes that run them. Consumers search real-time availability by location, sport and time and reserve in a few steps through the ATC Sports mobile apps and web app, with online payments guaranteed via Mercado Pago. Clubs use the ATC management software to handle online reservations, cash control, reporting and service sales. ATC operates across eight-plus countries including Argentina, Peru, Chile, Uruguay, Panama, Mexico, Colombia, Costa Rica and the United States, spanning 500-plus venues and more than 200,000 active players. The company is a 500 Global (500 Latam) portfolio company. It exposes no public developer API, SDK or developer portal at this time; this profile tracks its public web presence.

providers.name: FanCraze
providers.description: FanCraze is an International Cricket Council (ICC) officially licensed platform for cricket collectibles, trading, and fantasy gaming, serving more than 500,000 cricket fans worldwide. Its flagship products are Grails, a digital collectibles experience where fans pull officially licensed ICC player cards (Common through Legendary), trade them with other fans, and complete themed sets; and Matchday, a free-to-play fantasy cricket game where fans build squads from their collectibles and compete on live challenges tied to real ICC tournaments including Men's and Women's Cricket World Cups, T20 World Cups, and U-19 World Cups. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and is backed by investors including Tiger Global, Sequoia, Coatue, Dapper Labs, and Coinbase Ventures. FanCraze operates as a consumer (B2C) mobile and web app and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures its public web identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Supponor
providers.description: Supponor is a virtual advertising technology company for live sports broadcasting, now part of TGI Sport. Its software digitally replaces and inserts in-venue brand placements with real-time overlays, letting broadcasters serve region-targeted advertising across multiple feeds, languages, surfaces, and camera angles. Core products include AIR, an AI-driven virtual advertising platform for live broadcast; HUB, a pre-event suite for fixtures, inventory, playlists, creative and approvals; and Data Room, a post-event analytics platform for reporting, video storage, and performance metrics. Supponor works across any sport and surface with remotely deployable, all-weather technology, and is used by organizations including FC Bayern, the NHL, The FA, Serie A, and La Liga. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Northzone; it publishes a corporate and careers web presence but no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Hudl
providers.description: Hudl is a Lincoln, Nebraska sports performance and analytics technology company founded in 2007. The company started as a video sharing and review platform for high school, college, and professional teams and has grown into a global provider of video capture hardware, performance analysis software, and sports data services. Hudl operates across basketball, baseball, football, ice hockey, rugby, soccer, softball, and volleyball, serving customers from youth clubs through professional leagues. The company's product portfolio spans the core Hudl video platform, Hudl Focus AI-powered capture cameras (Indoor, Outdoor, Flex, Point), Hudl Replay and Hudl Studio for live and tactical analysis, Hudl IQ for American football analytics, Volleymetrics, the Hudl TV livestreaming product, and Hudl Tickets digital ticketing. Through acquisitions Hudl has consolidated several leading performance analysis and football data brands under its umbrella, including Sportscode (performance analysis software), Wyscout (the largest soccer video and stats database), Statsbomb (advanced football analytics), Instat (video and scouting), WIMU and Titan (athlete tracking and wearables), and Signal and ADI. Hudl exposes commercial developer surfaces primarily through Hudl Wyscout (Wyscout Data API, documented as OpenAPI 3.0 at apidocs.wyscout.com, with Database, Stats, Events, and Physical Data packs) and Hudl Statsbomb (the Statsbomb Aggregated API for player-match, player-season, team-match, and team-season data, accessed via the Data Hub, plus the Raw X&Y Tracking Data API and a Wyscout/Statsbomb ID Mapping API). Core Hudl video and Hudl Focus do not publish a public developer API; B2B integrations are sales-mediated. Hudl maintains a public GitHub organization (github.com/hudl) with infrastructure, resilience, and media tooling open source projects (Mjolnir, Fargo, HudlFfmpeg, react-native components), but these are engineering libraries, not product SDKs. Hudl's revenue model is SaaS subscriptions for video, analytics, and data packages, plus camera hardware sales and data licensing.

providers.name: TMRW Sports
providers.description: TMRW Sports is a sports, media, and entertainment company founded by professional golfers Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy, with Mike McCarley as Founder and CEO, focused on building modern, tech-forward approaches to live sports. Its ventures include TGL, a primetime team golf league played in partnership with the PGA TOUR; WTGL, a professional women's golf league; and a professional flag football league launching in partnership with the NFL. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners, TMRW Sports operates consumer sports and entertainment properties and does not publish a public developer platform, API, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Project Admission
providers.description: Project Admission is a ticketing technology company serving the live event industry — professional sports teams, leagues, artists, theaters, and venues. It layers on top of existing ticketing systems such as SeatGeek, Ticketmaster, and AXS to expand opportunities around the ticket and capture more value before, during, and after an event. Its platform provides branded storefronts, multi-channel inventory management, bulk ticket distribution, split season-ticket ingestion, and fan-engagement tools including influencer and group-sales programs. Project Admission does not publicly expose a developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile captures its verified public web and security surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Anthemis and Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Arc Simulations
providers.description: Arc Simulations is a London-based sports technology company, founded in 2022 by Henry Smith and Michael Armenakis and part of the Techstars London Spring 2024 accelerator cohort. Arc builds ball-tracking and simulation technology for cricket and other ball sports: professional-standard cricket balls carry embedded tracking tags that transmit position data to sensors up to 200 times per second, feeding a real-time simulation and analytics platform. The system predicts ball trajectory post-impact from velocity, angle and spin to deliver millimetre-accurate, autonomous feedback for every shot, with customisable field configurations that mirror live match scenarios. Arc serves players, coaches, scouts, analysts, broadcasters and fans through a hosted application (app.arcsim.io) and a player-facing app (player.arcsim.io) offering ball-by-ball 3D simulations. Arc's technology is built first for cricket but is designed to track nearly any sports ball. No public developer API, SDK, or API documentation is published at this time; this profile captures the company's identity and web/security posture in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: BallerTV
providers.description: BallerTV (Baller, Inc.) is a Pasadena, California sports media company that live streams and provides on-demand replays and highlights of youth and amateur sports, including basketball, volleyball, soccer, lacrosse, softball, and football, from thousands of tournaments and showcases nationwide. Subscribers range from families following athletes to NCAA and professional scouts using the footage for recruiting and scouting. The platform includes a Game Finder for locating events, purchasable athlete highlight reels, and BTVision, an AI-powered ball-tracking streaming technology that improves the basketball viewing experience. BallerTV is a consumer streaming product delivered through its website and iOS/Android apps; it does not publish a public developer API or SDK program. This profile was surfaced as an index-ventures portfolio company and enriched from public web sources.

providers.name: DAZN
providers.description: DAZN is a global over-the-top live sports streaming service headquartered in London and owned by Access Industries. Launched in 2015 out of the former Perform Group, it streams boxing, football, MotoGP, UFC and other rights to subscribers across more than 200 countries and territories, and has expanded through the acquisitions of Eleven Group, Foxtel/Kayo Sports and ViewLift, alongside the DAZN Bet and DAZN Media brands. DAZN operates a large Node.js microservice estate on AWS and publishes open source engineering tooling (the Kopytko Roku ecosystem, dazn-lambda-powertools) from its GitHub organization, but it runs no public developer program: there is no developer portal, no API reference, and no machine-readable specification for the consumer platform APIs that power its apps.

providers.name: FTN Network
providers.description: FTN Network is a New York-based sports data, analytics, and content company founded in 2020 that helps fans, fantasy players, and sports bettors make smarter decisions. FTN operates the FTN Fantasy platform (ftnfantasy.com), publishing proprietary NFL charting data, projections, DFS ownership, and betting analytics through articles, livestreams, videos, and podcasts. FTN also sells a REST/JSON sports-data API covering NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, PGA, CFB, and CBB across CSV, mid-tier API, and enterprise white-label plans. The company went through the Techstars Sports Tech Accelerator (2022) and is backed by 11 Tribes Ventures.

providers.name: Drone Racing League
providers.description: The Drone Racing League (DRL) is a New York-based professional drone racing property founded in 2015 by Nicholas Horbaczewski, staging first-person-view (FPV) races in which pilots fly identical, league-built quadcopters - the Racer series - through three-dimensional courses in stadiums, arenas and landmark venues at speeds above 80 mph. DRL designs its own racing drones, timing and telemetry hardware, produces and distributes its race broadcasts across NBC, Sky Sports, ProSiebenSat.1 and streaming platforms, and operates the DRL Simulator, an FPV racing game on Steam, PlayStation and Xbox that feeds the Swatch DRL Tryouts esports pipeline used to recruit professional pilots. The company was acquired by Infinite Reality (now Napster) in April 2024. DRL publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API specification, and as of the 2026-08-04 enrichment pass its primary web properties (thedroneracingleague.com, drl.io) were not completing a TLS handshake.

providers.name: gameSense Sports
providers.description: gameSense Sports is a Denver, Colorado sports-technology company that builds interactive, HD video-based cognitive training tools for baseball and softball. Its core Skill Recognition Training (SRT) uses the scientifically validated method of visual occlusion to measure and teach pitch recognition, reaction time, and decision-making so athletes learn to "see" plays before they happen. The platform packages this as SRT, Mini SRT, the Hitter IQ Challenge, and Skills Camps, and serves individual athletes, coaches, parents, teams, tournament organizations, and training facilities. gameSense sells subscriptions directly to athletes (B2C) and partners with college programs, professional organizations, and youth-sports groups (B2B). The company was selected for the inaugural Techstars SportsTech Melbourne accelerator. Its web application is built on the base44 platform. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched by the pipeline; it does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Matchday
providers.description: Matchday is a consumer mobile platform for collecting officially licensed digital football (soccer) player cards and building a squad, surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). The product is a business-to-consumer collecting and squad-building experience delivered through its mobile apps and website at matchday.com. As of this enrichment pass, Matchday does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or documentation surface: probing api.matchday.com, docs.matchday.com, and developer.matchday.com returned no reachable developer hosts, and the marketing site is a single-page application. This profile therefore carries company identity plus a domain-security probe rather than API artifacts, and remains a lead to revisit if a public API surface is launched.

providers.name: fuboTV
providers.description: Fubo (fuboTV) is a live TV streaming service focused on sports, offering more than 100 live channels covering the NFL, NBA, MLB, soccer, Formula 1, NASCAR and major broadcast networks (ABC, NBC, CBS, FOX), alongside news, entertainment and on-demand content. The service includes cloud DVR, multi-device streaming and no-commitment monthly plans. fuboTV was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a direct-to-consumer streaming brand and does not publish a public developer API program; this profile captures its public web, legal, security and identity surface.

providers.name: Ring Radar
providers.description: Ring Radar is horse show management software for the equestrian industry, operating at ringradar.com. The web-based platform helps horse show organizers, managers, and exhibitors run competitions end to end - handling show entries, class scheduling, ring coordination, results, and exhibitor information. Ring Radar is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this profile the company runs a consumer web application (login and signup) but publishes no public developer API, SDKs, OpenAPI, or developer documentation surface that could be discovered.

providers.name: Sportlogiq
providers.description: Sportlogiq is a Montreal, Quebec-based sports analytics company that applies patented computer vision and machine learning to broadcast video to generate high-resolution player tracking, event, and performance datasets across ice hockey, soccer/global football, American football, and youth sports. Founded in 2015 by Olympic figure skater Craig Buntin and computer-vision PhD Mehrsan Javan, the company is led by CEO Mitchell Wasserman and employs roughly 75 people, including a research team of ~13 AI scientists with 180+ patents and publications. Sportlogiq describes itself as the global leader in hockey analytics, with adoption across the majority of NHL franchises, 150+ professional and amateur hockey clubs worldwide, international hockey federations and leagues (SHL, PWHL, IIHF), NCAA hockey programs, NFL franchises, and global football organizations — collectively serving 220+ clients. In November 2024 Sportlogiq acquired 8BY8, a sports video infrastructure platform that combines multi-angle video, data streams, and audio for officiating, coaching, and player health workflows. In January 2026 Sportlogiq was itself acquired by Teamworks, where it continues to operate as the AI analytics layer of Teamworks' broader operating system for sport. Sportlogiq exposes its tracking and event data to teams, leagues, broadcasters, and analytics partners through a private partner API and bulk data feeds; there is no public developer portal, no self-service signup, no published OpenAPI specification, and no public SDKs or open-source repositories. Access is sold as part of commercial contracts and integrated directly into partner workflows.

providers.name: FloSports
providers.description: FloSports is an Austin, Texas-based direct-to-consumer sports media and live-streaming company founded in 2006 by brothers Martin and Mark Floreani. It operates a network of vertical properties (FloWrestling, FloTrack, FloGrappling, FloRacing, FloHockey, FloRugby, FloFootball and more) that deliver live and on-demand event streaming, original programming, news, rankings, and results for underserved and passionate sports communities through a subscription model. FloSports surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures; enrichment probing found a consumer streaming site with no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI, well-known discovery documents, or SDK program at this time.

providers.name: Dream11
providers.description: Dream11 is India's largest fantasy sports platform, operated by Sporta Technologies Private Limited and part of the Dream Sports group founded in 2008 by Harsh Jain and Bhavit Sheth and headquartered in Mumbai. Launched as a freemium fantasy game in 2012, it lets 140 million-plus users draft virtual teams and compete in free and paid contests across cricket, football, kabaddi, basketball and hockey, scoring on the real-world performance of the athletes they pick. Dream11 is a consumer, mobile-first product with no public consumer API program; its engineering organization does maintain public open-source infrastructure (Kong rate-limiter and circuit-breaker plugins, the Odin deployment tool) on GitHub and publishes an engineering blog.

providers.name: Fox Corporation
providers.description: Fox Corporation is a U.S. media company whose portfolio includes Fox News Media, Fox Sports, Fox Entertainment, Fox Television Stations, and the ad-supported streaming service Tubi. Fox is a Fortune 500 consumer of cloud, AI, and media technology APIs (notably AWS as preferred AI cloud provider) but does not publish a public developer portal at the corporate level.

providers.name: UberSense
providers.description: UberSense was a Boston, Massachusetts sports-technology startup whose mobile app provided slow-motion video capture and analysis for coaching athletes, from recreational to Olympic and professional levels. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), UberSense was acquired by Hudl in September 2014 and its technology folded into Hudl's sports video analysis products. The ubersense.com website is now defunct (a decommissioned Heroku app) and the company publishes no public API surface.

providers.name: Liberty Media
providers.description: Liberty Media Corporation is a media and entertainment holding company headquartered in Englewood, Colorado, owning interests in a portfolio of assets across media, entertainment, and sports. Its primary holding is the Formula One Group, which encompasses Formula 1 racing operations and MotoGP motorcycle racing, alongside investments in companies such as Liberty Broadband, QVC Group, Atlanta Braves Holdings, and Liberty Live Holdings.

providers.name: Signify Group
providers.description: Signify Group is a London, United Kingdom-based ethical data science firm founded in 2017 by co-founder and CEO Jonathan Hirshler, applying machine learning, natural language understanding, and open-source intelligence (OSINT) to social and digital media data. Its flagship service, Threat Matrix, is widely regarded as the leading platform for detecting, analysing, evidencing, and actioning online abuse and fixated threats directed at athletes, clubs, leagues, player unions, federations, brands, and other public figures. Threat Matrix scans incoming public messages across X (Twitter), Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok in 39+ languages, uses "augmented intelligence" (AI speed combined with trained human analyst nuance) to triage racist, sexist, homophobic, anti-semitic, islamophobic, gambling-driven, and personally targeted abuse, and produces evidence-grade reports with network mapping that can be used by platforms, police, sponsors, and protection teams. Customers and partners include the Professional Footballers' Association (PFA), Kick It Out, the International Tennis Federation (ITF) and WTA Tour covering c.8,300 players, the International Ski and Snowboard Federation (FIS) protecting 1,000+ athletes and officials, the Badminton World Federation (BWF), the NCAA, and Japan's 2026 World Baseball Classic squad. Signify also operates ShareScore (media coverage and social buzz analytics), Sports Insights (fan engagement and athlete insight analytics), and Online Forensics (brand reputation, OSINT investigations, and risk assurance). Signify is a private services firm with no public developer API, no public SDKs, and no public GitHub organization; engagement is via direct sales and managed service contracts with rights-holders, leagues, federations, and enterprise clients.

providers.name: Caffeine
providers.description: Caffeine was a social broadcasting and live-streaming platform founded in 2016 by former Apple designers Ben Keighran and Sam Roberts, and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Greylock Partners. Built on a proprietary WebRTC-based real-time video distribution network, Caffeine positioned itself as a low-latency, social-first alternative to Twitch for gaming, entertainment, and — in its later years — live sports, partnering with roughly 200 sports organizations and reaching tens of millions of monthly users. The company published open-source broadcasting tooling under its caffeinetv GitHub organization (libcaffeine, caffeine-rtc, an OBS plugin, and the CaffQL GraphQL code generator) but never shipped a public, documented developer API program. Caffeine announced it was ceasing operations, and its web presence is now a shutdown notice; this profile is retained as an a16z portfolio lead and is archival rather than an active, integrable API provider.

providers.name: The Athletic
providers.description: The Athletic is a subscription-based digital sports media company founded in 2016 by Alex Mather and Adam Hansmann, offering in-depth, ad-light coverage of national and local professional and college sports through a large staff of beat writers and columnists. Acquired by The New York Times Company in 2022, The Athletic delivers written articles, newsletters, podcasts, and live coverage across its website and mobile apps. As of this enrichment pass The Athletic does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications; its GitHub organization contains only forks of open-source engineering tooling rather than any public API product.

providers.name: Alltricks
providers.description: Alltricks is a French online retailer specializing in cycling, running, and outdoor / mountain-sports equipment. Founded in 2008 and headquartered near Paris in Saint-Cyr-l'Ecole (Yvelines), France, the company sells bikes and frames, components and parts, apparel, footwear, nutrition, and accessories across France and multiple European markets. Alltricks operates as a direct-to-consumer e-commerce storefront at alltricks.fr and was an early Partech portfolio company. As of this pipeline run the company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or /.well-known/ discovery surface; this profile captures its identity and the domain-security posture of its production host.

providers.name: ARG
providers.description: GoodPeople (ARG) is a boardriding community platform and e-commerce brand for skiers and snowboarders, operating under the tagline "Where the boardriding family meets." It publishes freeride competition results and rankings across events such as the Freeride World Tour (FWT), the IFSA Freeride World Qualifier (FWQ), and the World Rookie Snowboard Finals, alongside a blog covering event highlights, athlete spotlights, and freeride footage. The company also runs an online shop selling apparel, accessories, and lifestyle products, with a sustainability program that plants one tree for every purchase. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. No public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Athletes First
providers.description: Athletes First is a full-service sports representation and management agency founded in 2001 and headquartered in Southern California, with additional offices in New York City, Gainesville, Austin, and Atlanta. The firm represents elite NFL players, coaches, front-office executives, collegiate athletes, and sports broadcasters, and operates specialized departments spanning football contract negotiation, career management, pre-draft preparation, talent marketing and brand building, broadcasting and new media, media development and sales, and properties and events. In February 2023, Mastry Ventures in partnership with General Catalyst acquired a majority stake in the agency. This profile was surfaced as a General Catalyst portfolio company (sector: consumer) and added to the API Evangelist network. Athletes First publishes no public developer, API, or technical surface.

providers.name: Betty Labs
providers.description: Betty Labs was the startup behind Locker Room, a live-audio app that launched focused on live sports conversations before broadening into general social audio. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, the company was acquired by Spotify in 2021, after which Locker Room was rebuilt into Spotify's live-audio product (Greenroom / Spotify Live). Betty Labs no longer operates as an independent company; its primary domain (bettylabs.io) now redirects to Spotify, and it publishes no independent developer portal, API, documentation, or other public developer surface of its own. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired-company lead with no active API footprint.

providers.name: Buzzer
providers.description: Buzzer was a mobile live-sports streaming startup founded in 2020 by Bo Han, formerly director of live content at Twitter. Its consumer app, launched in 2021, sold micropayment access — as low as $0.99 to $1 — to short in-game moments of live sporting events, targeting Gen Z fans who would not buy a full cable or league subscription. Buzzer secured streaming rights covering the NBA, WNBA, NHL, PGA Tour and ATP Tour, and raised roughly $44 million in total, including a $20 million Series A in June 2021 co-led by Sapphire Sport and Canaan Partners alongside a large group of athlete and team-owner investors. On 19 May 2023 the company shut down the direct-to-consumer app and pivoted to a business-to-business model branded "Powered by Buzzer", announced as API licensing, custom development and consulting for leagues, teams and networks streaming direct to fans. That offering never reached public availability: Buzzer ceased all operations on 30 June 2023, citing "recent fundraising developments and market dynamics". No public developer portal, API documentation, specification, SDK or package was ever published. The buzzer.com domain no longer hosts the company and now redirects to an Atom.com domain-for-sale listing. Retained in the network as a historical record of a defunct company; not an active API provider.

providers.name: DeporPrivé
providers.description: DeporPrivé is a Mexico-based sports e-commerce platform operating as a members-oriented "Sport Experience & Outlet" that runs flash sales and private, time-limited shopping events across more than 300 athletic brands including Adidas, Nike, and Salomon, with discounts reaching up to 70%. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Mexico, the company curates footwear, apparel, and accessories for running, cycling, swimming, football, and general fitness, and has grown into one of the largest sport-specific online retailers in the country, fulfilling around 1,000 packages per day across multiple sales channels. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public developer program, API, or documentation surface has been identified for this consumer retail brand.

providers.name: edisn.ai
providers.description: edisn.ai was an AI-powered fan engagement platform for sports and media, surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The enrichment pipeline found no public developer surface — no API, OpenAPI, SDK, package, or documentation, and no docs/developer/api subdomain ever archived. The domain expired on 2026-05-09 and is now in pendingDelete/clientHold with no DNS resolution; by 2024 it already redirected to fubo.tv. No provider artifacts could be captured because none exist to search or derive from.

providers.name: Endeavor
providers.description: Endeavor was a global sports and entertainment company representing talent and owning and operating events, with subsidiaries including WME, IMG, and UFC. Following the 2024 take-private transaction by Silver Lake and the separation of TKO Group Holdings (UFC and WWE), the remaining talent, media, marketing, and licensing businesses were rebranded as WME Group. This repository tracks Endeavor as a corporate entity; no public developer APIs are currently published.

providers.name: Endeavor Group Holdings
providers.description: Endeavor Group Holdings was a global sports and entertainment company that represented talent, owned and operated events, and provided licensing, marketing, and media services through subsidiaries including WME, IMG, and UFC. Following the 2024 take-private transaction by Silver Lake and the separation of TKO Group Holdings (UFC and WWE), the remaining talent representation, media, marketing, and licensing businesses were rebranded as WME Group, which now operates WME, 160over90, Pantheon Media Group, and IMG Licensing. No public developer APIs are currently published.

providers.name: Fan Controlled Football
providers.description: Fan Controlled Football (FCF) was a professional indoor American football league in which fans voted on play calls in real time through a mobile app, playing a fast, 7-on-7 format staged at Pullman Yards in Atlanta and streamed to social and live-video audiences. The league drew high-profile athlete and celebrity team owners and investors and positioned itself as a fan-interactive, tech-driven sports and entertainment property. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. FCF paused operations and its public web presence (fcf.io) no longer serves a live site, so it currently exposes no developer portal, documentation, or API surface.

providers.name: Fanatics
providers.description: Fanatics is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of softbank-vision-fund, thrive-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Kairos Sports Tech
providers.description: Kairos Sports Tech was a Belfast and Dublin based sports technology startup that built a team operations and communication platform for professional sports, integrating team planning, daily communication, and player management into one centralized system used by more than 100 football and rugby organizations. Founded by Andrew Trimble and Gareth Quinn and backed by Techstars, Kairos was acquired by Teamworks in January 2024 and its product was folded into the Teamworks Hub athlete operating system. The standalone kairostech.io site now redirects entirely to teamworks.com/hub/, and Kairos no longer operates an independent public API, developer program, or discoverable API artifacts.

providers.name: Locker Room *
providers.description: Locker Room was a live-audio social app for sports fans built by Betty Labs, a seed-stage startup backed by GV, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Precursor Ventures. Launched in October 2020, it let insiders and fans hold real-time voice conversations about sports. Betty Labs and Locker Room were acquired by Spotify in March 2021 and folded into Spotify Greenroom / Spotify Live, which Spotify has since discontinued. Locker Room no longer operates as an independent product and exposes no public developer API or portal; this profile is retained as a GV portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Malaeb
providers.description: Malaeb (ملاعب) is the #1 sports pitch and facility booking application in the MENA region, letting players discover and reserve stadiums, courts, and pitches around them across Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, and Oman. Backed by 500 Global, Malaeb connects players and venue operators through a consumer mobile marketplace. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or well-known discovery surface; its web presence is a WordPress marketing site fronting a React single-page application.

providers.name: MoreTickets
providers.description: MoreTickets (摩天轮票务), operated by Shanghai Juqitech, is a next-generation internet performance ticketing marketplace founded in 2015. The platform lets consumers buy and sell tickets to concerts, stage plays, musicals, and sports events through a transparent, competitive pricing marketplace with standardized ticketing services. It operates primarily as a consumer-facing web and mobile marketplace and does not publish a public developer API or open platform. The company is backed by Qiming Venture Partners and has raised a reported $108M in funding.

providers.name: Rei do Pitaco
providers.description: Rei do Pitaco is a Brazilian online sports betting, daily fantasy sports, and casino platform founded in 2019 and headquartered in Brazil. The service offers competitive sports odds, live in-play betting, daily fantasy sports contests, and casino games aimed at the Brazilian market. As a regulated iGaming operator its consumer web and mobile properties are geo-restricted outside Brazil (the primary domains return HTTP 451 to non-Brazilian visitors), and the company exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface. Rei do Pitaco is backed by Bullpen Capital and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-sourced company profile.

providers.name: SIQ Basketball
providers.description: SIQ Basketball is a Techstars-backed sports-technology company that builds a FIBA-approved, sensor-embedded smart basketball and companion mobile app that automatically tracks shooting mechanics, makes and misses, shot arc and other performance data to coach players. Its technology is now marketed under the Spalding brand as the Spalding TF DNA Smart Basketball, sold with an app subscription. The company operates as a direct-to-consumer product and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its network identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Super Sports Media
providers.description: Super Sports Media Group is an IDG Capital-backed Chinese sports-media company best known for holding the English Premier League broadcast rights in mainland China and operating consumer sports streaming and content services under the ssports.com brand. Its platform was subsequently absorbed into iQiyi Sports (爱奇艺体育), and ssports.com now redirects there. This is a business-to-consumer sports streaming and media-rights operation with no public developer program: no API documentation, developer portal, SDKs, OpenAPI, or open platform surface could be found during enrichment. Profile retained as a network company record.

providers.name: TeamUp Inc.
providers.description: TeamUp Inc. operates fanZ (fanzapp.io), a gamified football (soccer) fan-engagement mobile app for iOS and Android. fanZ combines fantasy football (fantaZ), social following of teams, leagues and players, prediction challenges and mini-games, a rewards system of points, badges and digital collectibles, an official merchandise store, and global leaderboards, plus news, match highlights and video content. The product is a consumer-facing mobile application operated by Wathbah for Information Technology and backed by 500 Global; no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Tennis Channel
providers.description: Tennis Channel is a United States-based cable television network and direct-to-consumer streaming service dedicated to tennis and racquet sports, including live coverage and highlights from the ATP Tour, WTA Tour, Grand Slam events, and related pickleball and padel programming. Alongside its linear TV channel it operates a subscription streaming product (Tennis Channel / formerly Tennis Channel Plus) delivering live matches, on-demand video, news, rankings, and instructional content across web, mobile, and connected-TV apps. It was surfaced as a portfolio-linked company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass Tennis Channel publishes a consumer streaming platform but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: The Icon League
providers.description: The Icon League is a five-a-side (small-sided) football entertainment league co-founded by former Real Madrid and Germany midfielder Toni Kroos and German streamer Elias Nerlich (Eliasn97), operated by The Icon League GmbH of Cologne, Germany (Amtsgericht Köln, HRB 117138). Played indoors in a US-style 14-team franchise format with two 12-minute halves and "Rulebreaker" mechanics designed to maximize attacking play, the league blends professional and amateur players and is distributed primarily through livestreams and social platforms to a young German-speaking audience. Season one generated more than 1.3 billion social-media impressions, and the league raised a €15M Series A (backed by HV Capital) to professionalize operations and expand across Europe. This is a consumer sports-and-media property; it publishes a public content website (teams, players, standings, matchdays, news, tickets, shop) but exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: The Players' Tribune
providers.description: The Players' Tribune is a sports-media company that gives athletes a platform to connect directly with fans in their own words, publishing first-person stories, essays, letters, and video from professional players across football, basketball, soccer, baseball, and other sports. Founded in 2014 and backed by GV and IVP, it operates as a digital publisher rather than an API provider: an enrichment probe of theplayerstribune.com found a public sports-content website with no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface (no docs/api/developer subdomains, no /.well-known/ metadata, no llms.txt). This profile captures the company identity and the results of a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: VICI Sports
providers.description: VICI Sports operates FanFest, a white-labeled fan engagement platform for the sports industry that "turns fan engagement into revenue" by recognizing every fan action across stadiums, homes, and bars and rewarding it automatically. The company reports 150+ activations with sports brands and 30M+ fans commercialized, with partners including AC Milan, the Premier League, Paris Saint-Germain, and Manchester City. Backed by Techstars. No public developer/API surface is currently published; the fanfest.vip site is a single-page marketing app with a contact form only.

providers.name: YouStake
providers.description: YouStake is a peer-to-peer sports staking and sponsorship marketplace, founded in 2013, that lets fans invest in skilled poker and esports players in exchange for a share of their tournament winnings. Players list their buy-ins and backers can stake them for as little as $20, structured as a person-to-person sponsorship agreement rather than gambling. The consumer platform has since rebranded and now operates as StakeKings (youstake.com redirects to stakekings.com), which also offers white-label staking-marketplace software to partners. It is a business-to-consumer web application with no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or published API documentation.

providers.name: National Football League
providers.description: The National Football League (NFL) is the premier professional American football league, comprised of 32 franchises divided between the AFC and NFC conferences. The NFL produces the Super Bowl and is the most-watched sports league in the United States. The league does not operate a public developer portal; statistical and play-by-play data feeds are licensed to partners (notably AWS, Amazon Web Services Next Gen Stats, Sportradar, and Genius Sports) and are not offered as a self-serve developer API.

providers.name: Sinclair
providers.description: Sinclair, Inc. is a diversified media company and a leading provider of local news and sports in the United States. The company owns or operates a large portfolio of television stations and is involved in original programming, digital media, technical services, and broadcast technology innovation through subsidiaries such as Dielectric, Bitpath, ONE Media, and CAST.ERA. No public developer API or technical documentation portal is currently available.

providers.name: Fantasy Akhada
providers.description: Fantasy Akhada is an Indian daily-fantasy-sports platform operated by Super Six Sports Gaming Private Limited (CIN U72900HR2019PTC083570) of Gurugram, Haryana, founded in 2020 by Amit Purohit, Sumit Kumar Jha, Sahil Ahuja, Amit Bhardwaj and Ankit Upreti, with cricket commentator Harsha Bhogle as brand ambassador. Users build virtual teams for real cricket, football, kabaddi, basketball and hockey fixtures and enter free and cash contests, with the platform taking a commission on entry fees; it marketed itself on the lowest commission rates in the category and claimed 3.5 to 4 million registered users. The product shipped only as a consumer iOS app and a sideloaded Android APK plus a React single-page web lobby - there is no developer program, public API, SDK, webhook surface or developer portal of any kind, and none has ever been published. As of the August 2026 probe the brand's own web presence is broken: www.fantasyakhada.com is a dangling CNAME to a deleted AWS ap-south-1 load balancer, the apex carries no address record, every backend service host referenced by the company's own JavaScript bundles has been withdrawn from DNS, and only stale static CloudFront/S3 builds remain. India's Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act 2025 banned real-money online games nationwide in August 2025.

providers.name: Soccer API
providers.description: Soccer API (soccer-api.com) is a Spain-contacted vendor marketing live football data — fixtures, live scores, match events, standings, teams, players, line-ups, statistics, head-to-head, odds, predictions, historical seasons and a real-time WebSocket feed — to developers building sports, fantasy, media and betting applications. The site went live in August 2026 and publishes documentation, coverage and pricing pages plus a small tutorial blog. Re-probed on 2026-08-27, the product is announced but not shipped: every one of those three pages carries the vendor's own notice declaring its contents placeholders pending a production specification, the documented base URL is the literal example host https://api.example.com/v1, the coverage matrix names no real competition, all paid prices read "$XX", and there is no sign-up, console, key issuance or machine-readable contract of any kind. Access is requested by WhatsApp or email.

providers.name: Duane Morris
providers.description: Duane Morris LLP is a Philadelphia-headquartered, full-service U.S. and international law firm founded in 1904 by Russell Duane, Steven Heckscher, and Roland S. Morris. Chaired by Matthew A. Taylor, the firm describes itself as "a law firm with more than 900 attorneys in offices across the United States and internationally" — with a U.S. footprint spanning the East Coast, Texas, the Mountain West, and California, plus international offices in London, Singapore, Vietnam (Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City), Shanghai, Myanmar, and joint ventures/alliances reaching Mexico and Latin America. An Am Law 100 firm since 2001, Duane Morris is known for depth in intellectual property (including patent prosecution and PTAB practice), trial and appellate litigation, real estate, corporate transactions, employment, healthcare, cannabis, and life sciences. The firm publishes an extensive LexBlog-powered thought-leadership network of more than 50 practice-area blogs, all of which expose RSS 2.0 feeds via the standard WordPress /feed/ convention. Duane Morris does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI spec, GraphQL endpoint, webhooks, status page, or developer portal; the GitHub organization github.com/duanemorris exists but has no public repositories. The firm's only machine-readable surfaces are the RSS feeds of its blog network.

providers.name: National Basketball Association
providers.description: The National Basketball Association (NBA) is the premier men's professional basketball league in North America, comprised of 30 franchises (29 in the United States and 1 in Canada). The NBA does not operate a public developer portal; statistical, scoring, and play-by-play data feeds are licensed through official partners (notably Sportradar and Genius Sports). The stats.nba.com endpoints are not officially documented as a public API.

providers.name: Crossfit
providers.description: CrossFit is a fitness brand and training methodology built around constantly varied, high-intensity functional movements that combine strength, conditioning, gymnastics, and weightlifting. The organization operates a global network of independently owned affiliate gyms, delivers a coaching certification and education program (the Level 1 through Level 4 courses and specialty seminars), and produces the annual CrossFit Games competition season. CrossFit was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer and affiliate web presence (gym finder, courses, store, Games results) but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API definition.

providers.name: WePlayed
providers.description: WePlayed builds AI-powered short-form video for college athletics, automatically turning full game and event footage into shareable highlight clips that athletic departments, sponsors, and fans use to engage audiences and power sponsorship deals. A Techstars Sports Accelerator company that raised a $2 million seed round, WePlayed partners with SIDEARM Sports to distribute highlights across collegiate athletics websites. As of this profile WePlayed does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Hinsta
providers.description: Hintsa Performance is a Finnish performance-coaching company founded by Dr. Aki Hintsa, applying methods developed over 30+ years working with Formula 1 drivers and elite athletes to help executives, leaders, and individuals achieve sustainable success. Its "Circle of Better Life" model combines Nordic wellbeing with performance principles proven in Formula 1, delivered as bespoke coaching programs across three segments (sports, businesses, and individuals). The company reports 3,500+ intensive executive coaching programmes delivered for 500+ organisations. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public API, developer portal, documentation, or discovery surface (.well-known, llms.txt) was found during enrichment — this is a non-API wellbeing/coaching business.

providers.name: Fanatics Holdings
providers.description: Fanatics Holdings, Inc. is a global digital sports platform that connects fans with the teams, leagues, players, and events they love. Founded in 2011 and led by Michael Rubin, the company operates across several business segments: Fanatics Commerce (licensed sports merchandise, e-commerce, and manufacturing), Fanatics Collectibles (trading cards and memorabilia, including Topps), and Fanatics Betting & Gaming (the Fanatics Sportsbook and online casino). It has no public developer API program or published API specification; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile surfaced from a16z's venture portfolio.

providers.name: Beryllium
providers.description: Beryllium was a Singapore- and Delhi-based sports and trading game development platform founded in 2018/2019 by Amay Makhija, best known for its consumer product Sixer — a fantasy cricket game where users bought "Up" or "Down" virtual stocks in professional cricketers, with prices moving on in-game batting, bowling, and fielding metrics. The company raised roughly $3.6M across two rounds, including a $3M pre-Series A in June 2021 led by Bullpen Capital with Genting Ventures and Velo Partners. Beryllium was acquired by Dream Sports (Dream11) in October 2023. As of this enrichment pass the company is defunct as an independent operator: sixer.gg no longer resolves in DNS, and beryllium.ai is a parked domain listed for sale on the GoDaddy/Afternic aftermarket. Beryllium never published a public API, developer portal, or SDKs, so there is no API surface for the API Evangelist network to catalog.
